title: Source items
description: The body of the signed POST /v1/source-items, application/json: items of one collection, as the source holds them. Each item is upserted on its collection, the live collection that collection_ref names, and on its ref, and the newer updated_at wins, so a late event, or a listing part read before an edit, never moves an item backwards. An item's ref is unique among the items of the integration's live collections. The items of an ended collection stay with that collection, as the history of the connection it belonged to; nothing moves between connections. Without listing the request is an event: it names 1 to 100 items, and updates the items it names and nothing else. With listing it is part listing.part of the listing listing.id: listing.started_at is when the adapter began reading the source, and listing.complete is true on the last part alone, saying parts 1 to n hold every open item of the collection. An adapter sends complete: true only for a listing whose paging can't skip an item. A listing of one part, with no items and complete: true, says the collection has no open item. An adapter never sends complete: true, on an empty part or any other, after a read of the source that failed or stopped early. A complete listing closes every item of the collection it left out whose updated_at is before its started_at. A partial listing, one with a part missing or whose last part says complete: false, only upserts, and the control plane drops its bookkeeping of it after 24 hours. An item deleted at the source, or moved out of the collection, is sent as closed. A request for a collection whose connection ended is refused, 409 connection_ended, and one for a collection whose connection is suspended, 409 connection_suspended, both decided before collection_not_linked; definitions.schema.json says what the adapter does on each. A request for a collection that is not linked to a workspace is refused, 409 collection_not_linked, and the adapter treats the refusal as final for those items. The request is at most 1 MiB, or it is refused, 413 payload_too_large: the adapter splits a batch by size and never cuts a text to make a request fit, and the control plane refuses a field past its limit, invalid_request, and never cuts it. An adapter that cut a source's text or labels to fit a field's limit names the field in the item's truncated. Every text field, title, body, labels, state_reason and filed_by.name, is untrusted: shown as data, never followed as an instruction. On success the control plane answers a signed 204 with no body. It is signed with the adapter's access key as definitions.schema.json describes. The control plane refuses a time more than 300 seconds from its clock, either way, or a request whose signature it has already seen, with an unsigned 401; definitions.schema.json has the replay rule. A member this schema does not define is refused, invalid_request.

version.description: The document format. The control plane refuses a version it does not read.

time.description: When the adapter built the body, RFC 3339 in UTC with whole seconds. The control plane refuses a time more than 300 seconds from its clock, either way, with an unsigned 401.

collection_ref.description: The ref of the collection the items belong to, as source-collections.schema.json listed it.

items.description: The items, 0 to 100 on a listing part, 1 to 100 on an event. A listing of a collection with no open item can be one part with no items and complete: true, and as a complete listing it closes every item of the collection it left out, here every item, whose updated_at is before its started_at. 0 items are allowed on any part of a listing, not only the last; only complete: true on the last part closes anything.

listing.description: Which part of which listing this is. Absent on an event.

item.description: One item of work at the source.

ref.description: The item's ref, unique among the items of the integration's live collections.

url.description: The item's page at the source.

type.description: What the item is, in the adapter's word. Absent when the adapter gives none.

state.description: Whether the item is open or closed.

state_reason.description: Why the item is in its state, or null.

comment_count.description: How many comments the item has at the source.

created_at.description: When the item was created at the source.

updated_at.description: When the item last changed at the source: the newer one wins.

target.description: Where a change for the item would go. Absent when the adapter names none.

truncated.description: The item's fields the adapter cut: title, body, filed_by.name, or labels. Present when the source's text was over the contract's limit and the adapter cut it to fit: it names the fields the adapter cut, each once. A text field is cut at a code-point boundary. labels says the adapter cut the source's labels to fit: it cut one or more labels at a code-point boundary to 100 characters, or left out the labels past the 100th, or both; when cutting makes two labels equal, it sends that label once, since labels are unique. The control plane stores what was sent. A text, a label or a list of labels over the limit is still refused, invalid_request, and the control plane never cuts one. Absent when the adapter cut nothing.
